name: Descension

lead: Descension is looksmaxxing slang for a decline in how someone looks between two points in time, the opposite of 'ascension'. It is usually shown with side-by-side photos, for example an adolescent photo against a current one, or a before and after a lifestyle change.

The appearance payoff is diagnostic: by lining up dated photos, people try to spot which variable moved (weight, skin, hair, sun exposure, a medication, posture or lighting) and then target that variable. No clinical research uses the term in this sense; it is a forum convention.

paras: Users post dated photo sets in threads titled with the word, often asking others to 'rate' the change. Common comparisons span years (for example 2021 to 2024) or are tied to an event such as a medication start, a sunburn, weight change or hair loss. Participants also argue about whether an apparent change is real or due to camera lens, lighting, angle or expression.

Descension threads can be emotionally heavy for posters and readers, and appearance judgments made from photos are unreliable because of lens distortion, lighting and angle. Nothing is ingested or done to the body by the practice itself; the risks lie in the habits or interventions blamed for the change, and in the distress such threads can cause.

angle.text: Descension threads serve as a dated record of how a face or physique changed and what was happening at the time. Members use them to link changes to habits or treatments and to debate whether a change is real or a lens and lighting effect [3][7].

lead: Descension is looksmaxxing slang for a person's looks getting worse over time. It is the counterpart of ascension, the community's word for a rise in looks, and it is most often seen in forum threads that set an earlier photograph beside a recent one and ask other members to rate the difference [1][2][3].

The term works as a diagnostic format. By lining up dated photographs, members try to identify which variable moved between the two images, such as body fat, skin condition, hair density, tan or sun damage, medication, sleep, or the photo conditions themselves, and then decide what to address or rule out [4][5][6].

Looksmaxxing itself is described by Wikipedia as a self-improvement practice that emerged on incel and manosphere message boards in the 2010s and spread to TikTok in the early 2020s, with 'ascension' listed among its core vocabulary [3]. Descension is not covered there as a separate concept, and no clinical research uses the word for appearance change. Related, better-studied topics include photoaging and the way camera distance changes how a face is rendered in a picture [7][8][9].

paras: In looksmaxxing slang a person 'descends' when their appearance is judged to have declined and 'ascends' when it improves [3]. Threads titled 'my descension' typically show photographs from a younger age beside current ones, sometimes with a short backstory, and invite replies rating each image [1][2].

Titles often use superlatives and name a specific period, such as a change between 2021 and 2024, or ask readers to rate the poster at an earlier age such as 13 or 14 [2][4]. The same word also appears as a label applied to other people, for example a thread about a woman whose looks changed after time in the sun [5].

Wikipedia traces looksmaxxing to the PSL forums (PUAHate, Sluthate and Lookism.net) of the 2010s, where members rated one another's looks, and notes that the practice moved to TikTok in the early 2020s, where it was often framed as self-improvement [3]. The descension format belongs to the older forum photo-rating tradition: the dated threads in the looksmax.org archive run from 2022 to 2025 and recur under similar titles [1][4][10].
No single originator of the term is documented. It appears as ordinary vocabulary in thread titles, alongside 'ascension', 'glow-up' style before-and-after posts and rating requests [1][2][3].

Posters name a range of causes. One thread attributes a woman's change in appearance to sun exposure [5]. Another is framed around the look of a person who used anabolic steroids over seven years [11]. A third links changes to a hair-loss medication course and collagen changes while pursuing hairline treatment [10].

Members also name ordinary factors such as weight gain and aging. Some argue that the apparent change is a lens or lighting effect rather than a real difference, while another thread is titled to say that lens distortion cannot explain a given descension [6].

sections.h: What research says about the underlying ideas
paras: Photoaging is the skin change produced by chronic ultraviolet exposure. Wikipedia describes UVB as damaging DNA in the epidermis and UVA as reaching the dermis, where it damages collagen and elastin, and lists wrinkles, pigment change, spider veins, loss of lip fullness and solar lentigines among the visible signs. It describes sun protection as the main primary prevention and topical retinoids, with tretinoin the best studied, as secondary prevention [7]. This is the process members point to when they attribute a decline to sun [5].

Camera geometry is the other frequently debated variable. Wikipedia's article on perspective distortion explains that perspective depends on the distance between camera and subject rather than on the lens, so close-range wide-angle shots enlarge nearby features, and that moderate telephoto lengths of about 85 to 135 mm are generally considered flattering for portraits [8]. A 2018 modelling study in JAMA Facial Plastic Surgery estimated that at 12 inches the nose appears about 30 percent larger in men and 29 percent in women than at an effectively infinite distance, with little difference at 5 feet; the authors describe a projection effect, and note the study was a model rather than a clinical series [9]. Members who point to lens effects in descension threads are making this kind of argument, though no study has examined forum photo threads [6].

No studies found. The word 'descension' appears in the medical literature only in unrelated anatomical and clinical senses, such as descent of the testis or of a nerve, and not for appearance change. Research on photoaging and on camera-distance distortion exists as separate topics [7][9].

Descension threads are a staple of the community's photo-rating culture. Proponents of the format say seeing change documented helps motivate corrective action and shows which interventions matter. Critics within the same forums point to photo conditions as a confound, and replies in these threads range from supportive to harsh [1][6].

Press coverage of looksmaxxing from 2023 to 2026, listed in Wikipedia's article, discusses rating culture and criticism that the community is judgmental and linked to body dysmorphia; commentators in that coverage describe the effects on young men, while some practitioners report social benefits [3].

claims.claim: Sun exposure can cause a rapid, visible decline in looks.
Apparent descension is sometimes a camera or lens effect.
Steroid use can age the face noticeably within years.
Hair-loss drugs can cause facial change such as collagen loss.
Before-and-after rating threads help people find what to fix.
Face change from sun, weight or age can be partly addressed with skincare and sun protection.
